title: Mortal sin: turns from God, kills spiritual life, risks hell if death finds it
source_text: IV. Igitur existimant esse quaedam peccata quae cum charitate & amore Dei compati nullo modo possunt, & in quae homo cadere non potest, quin a Deo prorsus avertatur, & inimicus ejus fiat, atque sic in totum privetur vita spirituali, quae consistit in nostra cum Deo conjunctione, per gratiam ejus in nobis habitantem, & incidat in novum reatum gehennae & mortis aeternae; quam vitare nullo modo potest, si in eo peccato a morte deprehendatur, & nisi ante mortem, ex eo peccato, per novam Dei gratiam resurgat, & de novo Deo se reconcilietur. Itaque si quis justus talia peccata committit, excidit omnino justitia sua; nec amplius pro justo & sancto haberi potest: neque in eo reperitur sanctificatio illa, sine qua nemo videbit Dominum. Et haec sunt quae vocant peccata lethalia; quia sunt veluti quaedam plagae lethales, quae mortem animae inferunt, vitam gratiae prorsus in ea extinguentes, & hominem gehennae, quae mors secunda in Scripturis dicitur, reum constituentes.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore they judge that there are certain sins which can in no way be compatible with the charity and love of God, and into which a person cannot fall without being wholly turned away from God and becoming His enemy, and thus being entirely deprived of spiritual life, which consists in our conjunction with God through His grace dwelling in us, and falling into a new liability to gehenna and eternal death; which he can in no way avoid if he is caught by death in that sin, and unless before death he rises again from that sin by a new grace of God and is reconciled to God anew. And so if a just person commits such sins, he falls altogether from his righteousness and can no longer be held for just and holy; nor is that sanctification found in him without which no one will see the Lord. And these are what they call lethal sins; because they are like certain lethal wounds which bring death upon the soul, utterly extinguishing the life of grace in it, and constituting the person guilty of gehenna, which in the Scriptures is called the second death.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors treat mortal sin as incompatible with charity: it turns the soul from God and kills spiritual life.
If death finds such a sinner unraised by new grace, hell follows—and even the formerly just lose their standing.

choices.why: Roman synonym for mortal sins as soul-killing.
